thesis:
The page already runs three real simulations: FIG.1 (a 1D string), FIG.2 (a 2D fluid) and the LOUD rigid bodies. My five showpieces finish the specimen book with the conventions it still lacks: a character-set page, H&J (hyphenation and justification), an endpaper, a proof view and a performance. Each one is an exact simulation with a print metaphor. Each shows a live mono readout that proves it is real: wave energy, Knuth–Plass demerits, conserved area. Each settles back to a readable rest state, so it stays coherent rather than becoming a pile of effects.

Ranked by wow per risk:
1. FIG.4 Membrane. The character set is a 2D drum skin laid out as a designspace map.
2. FIG.3 H&J. The manifesto is justified on the wdth axis with live Knuth–Plass breaking and a draggable measure.
3. Overture. The specimen performs itself as one 32-second take, scroll as timeline, sequenced to the existing sounds.
4. Keyline. A proof and outline view with its grid, live metrics and pigment contours. This is the lead's X-ray seed, improved.
5. Endpaper. Vector mathematical marbling of the wordmark that un-marbles exactly. REWIND reuses it.

None of the five needs a second WebGL context: the marbling is vector 2D canvas, and the only GPU addition is a branch in the pigment display shader.

Build split:
- Stage D (self-contained, safe while stage C is in flight): Membrane, H&J, Keyline, plus upgrades 1–5.
- Stage E (needs stage C's final LOUD, rewind and sound APIs): Overture, Endpaper, plus upgrade 6.

Folios grow from /06 to /08: 04 Character set, 08 Endpaper.

Reserve if a slot frees up: a Scanimation acetate. This is a barrier-grid print trick: a static interlaced canvas of the instance ramp animates under a draggable striped sheet. It costs nothing per frame but needs device-pixel snapping.

Note for every new control: use U+25B8 (▸), not U+25B6 (▶). iOS renders ▶ as an emoji, and the page has a no-emoji rule.
upgrades_to_existing: 1. INK GAIN: the pigment has weight. Wet IKB fattens the type it lands on (up to wght +260 and wdth +6), and the type slims back as the pigment dries. Plucked hero letters also stir the fluid: inject velocity from each letter's wave velocity. Implementation: a tiny reduce pass renders dye into a 64×36 RGBA8 FBO. On WebGL2, read it back asynchronously (readPixels into a PIXEL_PACK_BUFFER, fenceSync, poll clientWaitSync(fence,0,0), then getBufferSubData), so there is no stall. On WebGL1, use a sync readPixels of that tiny FBO every 3rd frame. In 2D mode, sample the blot list analytically. Consumers are the hero letters (already written per frame), tagline words, manifesto word spans, tape words and Membrane cells. Write only on a delta above threshold. This is the most 'how did they do that' upgrade on the page: the brush and the type become one system. Risk 3–4.

2. REWIND replays your hand. During the 2.4s flight to the top, re-splat the visitor's logged strokes (they are already stored in document coordinates) newest-first as each one's y passes through the viewport. The page remembers where you touched it on the way back up. Mark them as ghost splats so the Anthropometry stats don't double-count. Risk 2.

3. MONOGOLD SEAL. The gold No.02 seal becomes a button, 'Brush: IKB / Monogold'. In Monogold mode, set X = PIG.XB on paper: by the inversion this gives #D4AF37 gold leaf, and ink type turns blue, which is Klein's own pair. Add three lines to the display shader: square leaf seams on a jittered 48px lattice with slightly darker 1px overlaps, Voronoi crackle, and a narrow specular glint whose angle follows the pointer. The Anthropometry plate prints those strokes in gold. Typing 'gold' or 'klein' anywhere is just an alias for this control. Gold still arrives only through the inversion, so the palette rule holds. Risk 2.

4. CHRONOPHOTOGRAPH. Strikes, big plucks and LOUD flings leave Marey-style multiple-exposure echoes. Keep a pool of 6 clones per letter, stamped every 40ms with the current axes and transform as 1px IKB keylines (-webkit-text-stroke, transparent fill), fading over 500ms. Kinetic type's 1880s ancestor, built from about 40 pooled spans. Risk 2.

5. INSTANCES PLOT BECOMES A HANDLE. On desktop the board pin has an empty middle-right area between the stage copy and the small plot. Enlarge the designspace plot to about 360px and make its dot draggable. Dragging flaps all tiles continuously to that exact (wdth, wght) with a live readout and ticks. On release it springs back to the scroll stage. Viewers get to be the type designer for a moment. Risk 2.

6. PLAY THE PLATE. Add '▸ Play your plate' on the Anthropometry print. A playhead scans the print left to right in 6s. A 64×7 occupancy grid (one getImageData on the plate canvas) plucks the pentatonic strings by row, and pigment under the playhead flashes gold. Clicking it turns sound on, because the click is the user gesture. The visitor's painting becomes a piano roll. Risk 2.

7. KINETIK CASE CASTS A METAL SORT (only if budget remains). In case 05, a 'Cast' button renders the playground's first letter as a raymarched lead type sort: mirrored relief, body with nick and shoulder, IKB ink on the face. Pipeline: rasterize the letter on canvas (nearest stretch keyword, exact weight), compute a CPU EDT signed distance field at 256² (about 6ms per cast), then raymarch 64 steps at half resolution with a beveled shoulder (d2 − (top − z)·tanθ), soft shadow and AO. Drag to turn it. It needs a second WebGL context, so create it on open and loseContext() on close. The rest of the page is paused under the dialog, so the GPU budget is free there. Wow 8, risk 6.

moves.name: FIG.4 MEMBRANE: the character set as a drum skin
moves.where: New section between 4B—03 Text and In Use: '4B—04 Character set ……… 96 glyphs' (folios become /08). Desktop: a 4-column glyph inspector on the left and a 12×8 glyph grid on the right (cells about 75px at 1440). Phone: an inspector strip on top, then an 8×6 grid.
moves.experience:
This is the specimen's glyph-overview page, and the grid doubles as a designspace map. Column sets wdth from 50 to 150 and row sets wght from 100 to 900, so a still frame reads from whisper (top-left, Thin Compressed) to LOUD (bottom-right, Black Extended), matching the hero ramp.

The grid behaves like a 2D drum skin:
- Click or tap a glyph and a circular wave rings out across the alphabet. Glyphs swell and condense in rings, the crest flashes IKB, the wave bounces off the edges and dies out in about 2s.
- Dragging through the grid leaves a wake, like a finger through water. Scrolling in pumps a wave down from the top row.
- On desktop, any letter key pressed while the section is on screen strikes that glyph, so the keyboard becomes the mallet.

Behind the glyphs, a faint 1px IKB contour plot shows the wave field: 'FIG.4 MEMBRANE · 12×8 NODES · c 10 · ζ 1.4'. The left inspector shows the last touched glyph huge, with font-editor apparatus (cap, x-height and base lines, advance boundaries, LSB/RSB) and a live readout 'R · U+0052 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER R · W 132.0 · G 812' that rides the wave. With sound on, a strike plucks that row's pentatonic string, panned by column. The page's physics now escalate from string (FIG.1) to membrane (FIG.4) to rigid bodies (LOUD).
moves.implementation:
DOM: 96 fixed cells with contain:strict and fixed width and height, glyph centred, so axis changes never reflow a neighbour. Each cell gets its rest instance in CSS from inline --c/--r: font-stretch: calc(50% + var(--c)*9.09%); font-weight: calc(100 + var(--r)*114.3). This makes the grid correct with JS off. During motion, JS overrides with font-variation-settings.

Simulation: Float32Array h, v, f; fixed substep 1/240 with an accumulator.
  lap = h[L]+h[R]+h[U]+h[D] − 4h   (Neumann edges: a missing neighbour = self)
  v += (C2·lap − K0·h − Z·v + f)·hs;  h += v·hs     with C2=100, K0=4, Z=1.4
  strike(i): v[j] += 9·exp(−d²(i,j)/1.4)
  wake: cells within 1.5 cells of the pointer get f += .015·speed·(1 − d/1.5)
  scroll: f[row 0] += F.vel·.002
  map: W = clamp(W0 + 55h, 50, 150); G = clamp(G0 + 420h, 100, 900)
  write only if |ΔW| ≥ .5 or |ΔG| ≥ 4 (quantising also raises glyph-cache hits)
  crest: toggle class 'hot' (IKB) when v > 2.2, off below 1.2 (hysteresis; class toggles, no colour writes)
  sleep when Σ(h² + v²) < 1e−4 and there is no input

Contour: a 2D canvas behind the grid runs marching squares at level .35 on a bilinear 48×32 upsample of h, redrawn only while the system is awake.

Inspector: one big glyph span mirrors the active cell's W/G each frame. Metric lines come from one canvas measureText at layout.

Keys: keydown counts only when the section is at least 50% visible and the target is not a field. Ignore Space, arrows, PageUp/PageDown and Tab so scrolling still works. e.key strikes its cell.

Accessibility:
- The section has a heading and a one-line description.
- The grid is aria-hidden; a single roving-focus control sits over it. Arrows move the active glyph and Enter/Space strike it.
- A throttled polite aria-live region announces 'R, wdth 132, wght 812'.

API: K2.membrane.strike(ch).
moves.phone:
8×6 = 48 glyphs (A–Z, 0–9, & @ ? ! § ¶ € $ # % * +) in 44px cells.
- Tap strikes. The grid is data-nodrop, so a tap does not also drop pigment.
- A horizontal swipe makes a wake: touch-action is pan-y on the grid, so vertical scroll stays native and still pumps the top row.
- The inspector collapses to a 120px glyph plus one mono readout line above the grid.
moves.perf_and_fallback:
Worst case is about 96 font-variation writes per frame during a ring. Each cell is a contained box, so each write costs a style recalc, a one-glyph layout and a paint: expect 2–4ms on desktop; phones have only 48 cells.

Governor: if dt stays above 22ms for 10 frames, interlace the writes (even cells on even frames, odd cells on odd frames). The section is IntersectionObserver-gated and sleeps at rest.

Fallbacks:
- Reduced motion: a static designspace map; a click only sets the inspector.
- No JS: the static designspace grid.
- Glyph coverage: check once by comparing canvas measureText against the .notdef width (U+FFFF), and drop any glyph Anybody lacks.

moves.name: FIG.3 H&J: the manifesto justified on the width axis (live Knuth–Plass)
moves.experience:
The manifesto is fully justified with perfectly even word spaces and no rivers, because each line is justified by its own wdth instead of by spacing. This is Zapf's hz-program idea, done with a variable axis.

The left margin lists each line's setting ('L04 · W 083.6 · G 520') with a tiny glue bar. The right edge carries a crop-mark handle, 'MEASURE 34 EM ⟷'. Drag it and the paragraph re-breaks in real time with optimal Knuth–Plass breaks: every line breathes to fill the new measure and the readouts tick.

The ink-up becomes an axis trade. As a line crosses the reading line its weight rises from 200 to 520 while its width falls in exact compensation, so the line inks up without changing length; the readouts show W falling as G rises. A line that cannot fit (rare, only at very narrow measures) gets TeX's black overfull slug in the margin, a joke for typographers.

Caption: 'FIG.3 H&J — JUSTIFIED BY WDTH, NOT BY SPACE · KNUTH–PLASS · Σ DEMERITS 1,204'.
moves.implementation:
Measure once per layout, with 4 batched reads: for (wd, wg) in {60, 120} × {200, 520}, set it on the

and read every word span's offsetWidth plus one space probe. This gives each word a bilinear model w(wd, wg) = a + b·wd + c·wg + d·wd·wg, exact at the corners; Anybody's widths are close to linear in wdth. A line i..j at weight g then has width A(g) + B(g)·wd (words plus spaces), so wd* = (M − A)/B. breaks(M) at g = 520: a DP over word boundaries (n ≈ 60, O(n²), about 2k evaluations): - a line is feasible if 60 ≤ wd* ≤ 120; - r = (wd* − 80)/20; badness = 100·|r|³; demerits = (10 + badness)²; - add 3000 when |wd* − wd_prev| > 22 (TeX-style fitness classes, so adjacent lines never jump in width); - the last line is ragged at wd 80 with demerits 0, plus a widow penalty if it holds one word. On a break change, re-parent the word spans into .ml line spans (nowrap) and set each line's 'wdth' wd* and 'wght' g. Ink-up: each frame, only lines whose g changed get wd = (M − A(g))/B(g). Residual: in the next read phase, read those lines' offsetWidth and take one Newton step, wd += (M − w)/B. It converges in 1–2 frames, invisibly. Handle: pointer capture on a 24px hit strip. Keyboard: role=slider with aria-valuenow in em; arrows move ±1em. Range: 55–100% of the column. The paragraph's height changes with the measure, so refresh Zones.measure() and measurePins() on drag end. Content below is off screen during a drag, so nothing visible jumps.
moves.phone:
Same engine. At 30px type on a ~358px measure there are only 4–6 words per line, so justifying with the axis is even more visible.
- The handle is a 28px strip on the right edge, with touch-action:none only there; the rest stays pan-y.
- Per-line readouts collapse into one mono row above the text: 'H&J · 14 LINES · WDTH 71–96'.
moves.perf_and_fallback:
About 60 words and 12 line spans: the DP and the writes take well under 1ms. The 4 measurement layouts run only on layout.

Fallbacks:
- Reduced motion: justification and dragging still work (they are direct manipulation, not animation); ink-up shows its end state.
- Missing wdth axis (fallback font, where widths at wd 60 and wd 120 are equal): text-align:left and the handle is hidden.
- No JS: the current ragged setting.

moves.name: OVERTURE: the specimen performs itself (32s, one take)
moves.experience:
Clicking turns sound on (the click is the gesture), and the folio flaps count in 1-2-3-4. The page then plays itself as one choreographed take at 120 BPM in A minor pentatonic. The scroll is the timeline.

The score, bar by bar:
- Bars 1–2: the hero letters are a 7-step sequencer. Every 8th note is a strike: punch to 150/900, a pigment burst and a Karplus–Strong note. Meanwhile a crop-mark ghost cursor labelled '4BOOSER · PLAYING' paints a pigment phrase on the beat.
- Bars 3–4: a glide through Strings (tapes plucked on beats 1 and 3) and Text (one line inks up per beat).
- Bars 5–6: In Use rows wipe blue on each beat from 01 to 05, each riso plate flashing.
- Bars 7–8: a filtered-noise riser while the camera zooms into the O. The ink lands on the next downbeat with a sub thud.
- Bars 9–12: one Instances stage per bar, flaps ticking in 16ths, the instance getting heavier as the music builds. The Flood comes on bar 12 as the filter opens.
- Bars 13–16: the LOUD letters drop on 8ths with letterpress thuds panned by x. 'LOUD.' lands on the bar-15 downbeat with all seven strings as a chord. The full stop rolls off on the last beat, then a ding and the toast 'Your turn.'

A hairline progress bar under the nav reads 'PERFORMING · BAR 09/16 · 120 BPM — any key to stop'. Any wheel, touch, key or click hands control back immediately, wherever the page is.

Idle variant: after 20s idle on the hero (only there, never mid-reading), the ghost hand plays a 2-bar riff in place with no scrolling, and the PERFORM chip pulses. This replaces the lead's idle-show and sequencer seeds.
moves.implementation:
Data:
  score = [[bar, beat, act, arg], …]
    e.g. [1,0,'strike',0], [1,.5,'strike',1], …, [5,0,'row',0], …, [7,0,'riser',4], …, [15,0,'chord',[0..6]]
  cam = [[0,'#top'], [3,'#strings'], [4,'#text',.6], [5,'#work'], [7,'#process',0], [9,'#process',1], [9,'#instances',0], [13,'#instances',1], [13,'#contact']]
    resolved to px at start from section offsets and pin runs; y(t) = smootherstep between keys

Clock:
  sound on:  t = ctx.currentTime − t0 − (ctx.outputLatency || ctx.baseLatency)
  sound off: t = (performance.now() − t0)/1000

tick(): y = cam(t)
  Lenis: lenis.scrollTo(y, {immediate: true, force: true}); otherwise window.scrollTo(0, y)
  fire visual acts whose time ≤ t
  schedule audio acts 120ms ahead with start(when), so they are sample-accurate

Abort: capture-phase wheel, touchstart, keydown and pointerdown (except on the stop control) → fade the master gain over 250ms, stop queued sources, hand back control.

It is built from existing K2 calls: hero.strike, strings.pluck, pigment.splat/burst, sound.pluck/tick/thud/ding/whoosh, scrollTo, and loud.* (from stage C). Pinned and scrubbed systems follow the scroll for free.

New small APIs:
- K2.rig.ghost(x, y, label | null): the rig follows a scripted Catmull-Rom path;
- K2.work.preview(i | −1): row wipe and card without a pointer;
- Sound.riser(dur) and Sound.chord(notes);
- K2.overture.play() and .stop().
moves.phone: Same score. It uses programmatic scrollTo each frame (there is no Lenis on touch), and the first touchstart stops it. The ghost cursor is a 6px dot with a chip, without crop marks. The menu has '▸ Perform'.
moves.perf_and_fallback:
There is no new rendering: Overture only calls existing systems, so it costs what normal scrolling costs. Visuals and audio share one clock, so they cannot drift.

Fallbacks:
- Audio refused or unavailable: it plays silently on the performance.now() clock.
- Reduced motion: the control is hidden; the page never auto-scrolls.
- Stage C APIs missing: the colophon bars fall back to loud.kick() plus thuds.
- Layout changes mid-run (resize): stop.

moves.name: KEYLINE: proof view (the live page in outline, with its grid and metrics)
moves.where: A page-wide mode. Toggled by a 'PROOF ○' nav button next to SOUND (in the menu on phones). Shortcut: G; letter keys go to the Membrane only while it is on screen. This replaces the lead's X-ray/grid seed.
moves.experience:
A 1px IKB scan line sweeps down the viewport and reprints the page as a designer's proof, like Illustrator's Outline view on a live site:
- All type becomes 1px keylines with transparent fill. Where the variable font keeps overlapping contours, they show inside the letters, so you see the font's construction while the hero still plucks.
- The 12-column grid and gutters appear as 6% IKB columns, and the text section shows its 8px baseline grid.
- Every display line carries a spec chip ('ANYBODY 264/238 · W 132 · G 812') that tracks live as letters move: hero, board tiles, LOUD bodies.
- Canvases show as wireframes with crossed image boxes.
- The Klein pigment draws as a topographic contour map instead of a fill.

Hovering anything (tapping on phones) draws Figma-style redlines: IKB distance lines with px labels to the parent edges and to the nearest neighbour. Toggling again reprints the page in ink with the same scan line.
moves.implementation:
CSS under html.proof: display and body type get color: transparent and -webkit-text-stroke: 1px var(--kl). --kl is ink on paper zones and paper on ink and IKB zones (keyed off the existing [data-nav] tones).

Sweep: document.startViewTransition(toggle), with ::view-transition-new(root) animating clip-path from inset(0 0 100% 0) to inset(0), plus a 1px IKB line riding the edge. Fallback: an instant toggle.

Overlay: one fixed 2D canvas (pointer-events: none, DPR capped at 2) draws:
- the grid, from the .wrap metrics;
- boxes and chips for [data-spec] elements, measured on toggle and on layout;
- live boxes (at most about 40 rects: hero letters, tiles, LOUD glyphs), re-read in the scheduler's read phase and drawn in tick.

Pigment display shader: add a uniform uProof. When it is on, a = 1 − smoothstep(0., 1., abs(fract(d·7.) − .5)/(7.·fw)), which turns the existing threshold-and-halftone fill into iso-lines of dye density.

Redlines: on pointermove, find the closest [data-spec] or block element. Read its rect, its parent's padding box and the nearest sibling's rect, then draw 4 dimension lines with mono px labels.
moves.phone: A menu toggle. In proof mode, a tap shows the redlines for the tapped block; a link needs a second tap to follow. The grid shows 4 columns.
moves.perf_and_fallback:
Stroked text paints slightly more. The overlay redraws only when something moves, and the mode is off by default.

Fallbacks:
- No View Transitions support: an instant swap.
- Reduced motion: no sweep, instant toggle.

Check that 1px ink keylines on paper hold at least 4.5:1 contrast. The mode lasts only for the session (sessionStorage, try/catch).

moves.name: ENDPAPER: FIG.6 mathematical marbling, exactly reversible
moves.where: A new last spread after the colophon content: a full-bleed paper sheet, about 90svh on desktop and 64svh on phones, titled '4B—08 Endpaper'. The REWIND bar moves to its foot.
moves.experience:
Specimen books close with marbled endpapers. Here the marbling bath holds 4BOOSER set in Black Extended (150/900), floating on paper.

As the sheet scrolls in, the page marbles it on its own in about 2.5s. IKB, ink and paper drops bloom along a line and push the letters into rings; a wavy comb then drags them into a classic gel-git pattern. The rest state is a crisp, vector-sharp marbled sheet in the brand's three inks.

Interaction:
- click or tap drops ink, cycling IKB → ink → paper;
- drag combs with a stylus;
- a mono readout proves the maths is exact: 'OPS 027 · AREA 100.00% · INVERTIBLE'.

Then the trick: '⟲ UN-MARBLE' plays every operation backwards, and the chaos unswirls into the original letters, perfectly crisp. REWIND uses the same move: the endpaper un-marbles first (1.2s), then the page flies to the top.

The inks stay inside the palette: IKB, ink and paper. There is no gold, because static gold is reserved for the seal.
moves.implementation:
Vector, not pixels, following Jaffer / Lu et al. 2012, 'Mathematical marbling'. Inks are closed polylines (Float64Array) in z-order, filled with 'evenodd'.

Type: rasterize '4BOOSER' on canvas at 'extra-expanded 900' (the 150/900 instance is exactly reachable in canvas). Trace it with marching squares, simplify with RDP at ε .5px, and resample to at most 3px spacing. Holes are just extra rings.

Operations and their inverses:
  DROP(c, r):   p ← c + (p − c)·√(1 + r²/|p − c|²); push circle(c, r, 128 points) as the top ink
    inverse:    p ← c + (p − c)·√(1 − r²/|p − c|²)
    animation:  drops compose in r², so apply √(r_k² − r_(k−1)²) each frame
  TINE(B, M, z, λ):  d = |(p − B)·N|;  p ← p + z·λ/(d + λ)·M
    inverse:    p ← p − z·λ/(d + λ)·M   (exact, because the shear leaves d unchanged)
  COMB:   the same, with d ← s/2 − |(d mod s) − s/2| (wavy tines, still exact)
  STYLUS (one finite drag segment): δ(p) = z·λ/(d + λ)·M·w(s), with s = (p − B)·M and w a smooth window on [0, L]
    inverse:    3 Newton steps on s (one-dimensional and monotone)

After each operation:
- refine: insert a midpoint wherever a segment exceeds 3px, capped at 80k points;
- area: shoelace sum per ink, which feeds the readout.

Render: fill paper, then ctx.fill(Path2D(rings), 'evenodd') for each ink in z-order. DPR capped at 2. Redraw only while an operation is animating.

Un-marble: run the operations in reverse through their inverses over 1.2s with acceleration. Remove each drop polygon as its operation is undone. Finally restore the saved original rings, so the rest state is bit-exact.

API: K2.marble.unmarble() → Promise, called by REWIND.
moves.phone: Tap drops ink. A horizontal swipe combs; touch-action is pan-y on the bath, so vertical scroll stays native. The un-marble button is full width. The vertex cap drops to 40k.
moves.perf_and_fallback:
There is no WebGL, just a 2D canvas, so no second context. Each operation step costs about 0.5ms of vertex maths; the fill costs 2–5ms at 60k points. At rest it costs nothing (IntersectionObserver gating plus sleep). The bath is data-nodrop, so pigment never fights the marbling.

Fallbacks:
- Reduced motion: the marbled state is computed instantly and shown still; un-marble swaps between states instantly.
- Canvas failure: a still endpaper with 4BOOSER typeset.

reject: GLOBAL AXIS MIXER that remixes ALL typography: it fights the thesis. Every instance on the page is deliberate: the hero ramp, each client's title in its own voice, the board stages. Widening everything breaks the fitted measures and forces a full refit on every knob tick (layout thrash). It also needs a global offset contract across every system that writes font-variation-settings per frame. The scroll is already the page's crossfader from whisper to LOUD. Axis control belongs where it means something: the Kinetik pad, the Membrane inspector and the draggable Instances plot (upgrade 5).

NIGHT PRESS as a dark mode that follows prefers-color-scheme by default: the spec sets a single deliberate light look. The colour maths is hard-coded in the riso plates, flap shades, flood, plate tooth and the pigment X/XB, so a dark mode doubles QA for every system. The page already prints on black stock from Threshold through Instances. At most it could be a hidden egg, and it is not worth a stage.

LETTERPRESS PLATEN between sections, and PAGE-WIDE TRANSITIONS BETWEEN EVERY SECTION: they add scroll length and repetition, and dilute the two signature transitions (the O zoom and the flap flood). In Swiss rhythm the plain edges are the rests. Impression shading and ink spread can live on the LOUD letter landings instead.

IDLE SHOW that takes over the page after about 20s of idle: it would auto-scroll a visitor who is reading the manifesto or a case, which is hostile. Replaced by Overture: a full performance only on an explicit click, and only an in-place ghost riff when idle on the hero.

KONAMI CODE → LOUD MODE with screen shake and bass: shake is a vestibular accessibility problem and a cheap gag on a page that otherwise earns its loudness. Typed 'klein' and 'gold' survive only as aliases for real controls (the Monogold seal).

CURSOR GLYPH TRAIL / TYPE BRUSH variants: a 2015 cliché, and a second brush competes with the concept of one living brush (Klein pigment). The Chronophotograph upgrade gives the motion-trail feeling in a way that belongs to the specimen.

VELOCITY-BASED GLOBAL TYPE STRETCH while scrolling fast: a generic effect. It breaks fitted measures, stacks on top of the systems that already react to scroll velocity (string, tapes, riso slip), and makes fast scrolling unreadable.

STANDALONE HERO SEQUENCER with tempo from scroll speed: scroll velocity is too jittery for a tempo, and sound is opt-in, so few would hear it. The 7-step hero sequencer lives inside Overture at a fixed BPM, where it has a score.
HELLBOX OF DISCARDED LETTERS as its own feature: fold it into stage C's LOUD physics (letters knocked loose collect in a hellbox tray on the floor shelf). It does not justify its own build.

thesis:
Depth comes from one grammar, not a pile of effects. Every hidden layer is a real print-shop or specimen-book convention: a key, a proof, errata, footnotes, a contents page, a thumb index, a composing stick, a job case and a hellbox.

**How it is organised**
- **Shortcuts are punctuation that means its action:** `?` key · `#` grid · `!` loud · `.` full stop · `@` email · `^` back to top · `[` `]` pages · `+` `−` turn it up or down.
- **Typing is a verb:** every word you type is set in type and can be printed in Klein pigment.
- **Discoveries are countable:** each one drops a sort into a 12-compartment job case ("05/12 sorts"), so the depth is visible instead of secret.

**Four spine items make the rest discoverable.** Build them first within their stage:
- the Key sheet (#7);
- the job case (#10);
- proof mode (#13), which shows the machinery, including the single sleeping rAF scheduler, to a developer jury;
- the composing stick (#18), which hosts the eggs.

Everything else is a micro-reward hung on an element that already exists: readouts, seal, clock, folio, running heads, footnotes, tiles, plot and plate. All of it is tuned to the hero's pentatonic instrument.

**House rules for every item**
- Overprint, never withhold. A still frame is always legible, and nothing waits at opacity 0.
- One table-driven keydown dispatcher. The Key sheet is rendered from the same table, so the docs cannot drift from the keys.
- Keys are matched on `e.key` first, then `e.code` + `shiftKey`. The owner types on a Russian layout, where `#` and `@` sit elsewhere.
- One new pigment primitive (a texture "stamp") powers word printing, the TYPE brush and the KLEIN flood.
- Reduced motion keeps every direct manipulation and drops all autonomous motion.
- Phones get every feature through tap, long-press or the menu. Nothing is hover-only.

**Suggested build split**
- **Stage D (spine):** dispatcher and Key sheet, composing stick with stamp and magic words, job case, proof mode, running-head prints, contents and thumb index, sound map and VU meter.
- **Stage E (micro layer):** jokes, developer layer, footnotes, selection inspector, metrics, seal, clock and monogram, scrub and charge, LOUD and WHISPER, plate, instances, manifesto, autopilot, brush tips, strings index.

The moves below are ranked by wow ÷ risk, so the cheap wit comes first.
upgrades_to_existing: **Post-flood IKB void.** About 650px of bare IKB sits at the end of the Instances pin, before 4B—06 (qa2-c-base-desktop-s75). It is the biggest dead area on the page. Ask stage C to start the LOUD letter drop as the flood completes, so the void becomes the fall shaft and letters visibly fall through it onto the shelves. Either way, hang the 'This page intentionally left blue.' wall label there (move 1).

**Rig chips repeat visible labels.** The CLOSE chip sits under 'Close ✕' in qa2-a2-d-case, and SOUND ON under the Sound toggle. On buttons that already show their label, make the chip show the keyboard shortcut instead (ESC, !, @, ^, 1–6). That turns redundancy into a free tutorial.

**Hero readouts (W 061 / G 189) are display-only.** They are the most-looked-at mono on the page. Make them scrubbable sliders (move 16): they become the first thing people play with, and the title page becomes keyboard-operable.

**Instances board, desktop:** about 650px of empty ink between the stage copy and the designspace plot (qa2-a2-d-board-flap). Fill it with a waterfall of the current instance at 9/12/18/24/36px that re-sets with a flap cascade on each stage change (move 14).
**Colophon, desktop:** empty IKB under Elsewhere / Availability / Local time, beside the tall plate (qa2-a2-d-foot). The job case and the errata slip go there (moves 10 and 1).

**Anthropometry empty state** sends people elsewhere ('Move across the page to paint'). Let them paint on the plate directly. Hold-to-replay and the PAPER / BLACK / LEAF stock switch make the plate a reward for people who did paint (move 12).
**Footnote marks (*, †, ‡) are dead ends.** Give them hover text in the rig chip, a jump to the note with a proof circle, and an exact '↩ back' link. Secrets append live § notes (move 5).

**The No.02 seal is the only Monogold object, and it is inert.** Add a coin flip on hover, a blind-emboss stamp that shakes the forme, and 5 taps to trigger LOUD, which is also the phone path to the Konami egg (move 6).
**The nav folio is passive text.** Make it the Contents button: a ramped table of contents with a flap-through page turn (move 9).
**Running heads and closing folios are static rules.** Print events give the three consecutive paper sections (Strings, Text, In Use) a transition each, without a set piece (move 8).
**The FIG.2 caption is static.** Make it a live pigment readout from Pigment.stats() ('12 strokes · 3 drops') and the brush selector (move 20).

**Sound is good but sparse** (pluck, tick, thud, ding, whoosh). Route row hovers (the index plays a scale), nav links, running heads, the stick, secrets and footnotes through it, and add a 7-bar VU meter. Sound-on then feels like an instrument, not occasional effects (move 11).
**The calibration line counts a single %.** Have it list the real font files from document.fonts ('ANYBODY 2/2 · ARCHIVO 1/1 · PLEX 2/2'): more apparatus in the same 1.6s.

**Pigment colour over IKB areas (XB) already maps paper to #D4AF37 Monogold.** So GOLD mode is just a lerp of PIG.X toward PIG.XB, which is uploaded every display frame. No shader change is needed, which makes it nearly free.

moves.name: Typographic jokes pack: 'intentionally left blue', errata slip, forgery stamp
moves.where: Post-flood IKB void (end of the Instances pin); colophon beside the plate; nav 'Specimen No. 02' label; plate signature input
moves.experience:
(a) The bare IKB at the end of the flood gets a museum wall label, bottom-left:
- 'This page intentionally left blue.' in Anybody 50/300;
- under it, in mono: 'Untitled Blue Monochrome (4B 191), 2026 · Pure pigment on scroll · 1440 × 652 px', with live dimensions.

(b) An ERRATA slip (paper, 1px ink rule, rotated −1.5°, half tucked under the plate frame). It straightens on hover. Lines:
- 'p.01 For whisper read WHISPER.'
- 'p.04 Plate 03 printed 1px out of register. Stet.'
- 'p.05 The O is shown at ~70× actual size.'
- 'p.06 For K _ _ _ _ read the blue.' (a hint for a secret)

(c) Hovering 'Specimen No. 02' shows the chip 'No. 01 is out of print'.

(d) Signing the plate 'Yves Klein', 'Klein' or 'YK' slams an IKB rubber stamp FORGERY across the print, with the toast 'The Klein estate has been notified.' This counts as a secret.
moves.implementation:
Static markup plus about 40 lines of JS. - **(a)** An absolutely positioned

in the flood pin's last viewport (bottom/left gutters). It sits on the identical blue band, so it also reads in reduced motion. The px values are written in K2.onLayout from F.vw/F.vh. - **(b)**

in the colophon grid, placed under the plate frame by z-index. Transform rotate, with a 300ms transition to 0 on hover or focus-within. - **(c)** data-cursor-label on the label span. - **(d)** In Ant's signature input handler: normalise (trim, lowercase, strip dots), then test /^(yves )?klein$|^y\.?k$/. On a match, add the .forged class: an Anybody 150/900 uppercase stamp, 3px IKB border, rotate −12°, a 'scale 1.6→1' slam keyframe, mix-blend multiply. Also call Sound.thud(.5, .9) and K2.secrets.unlock('forgery'). Clearing the field removes the stamp.
moves.phone:
All of it works.
- The void label sits bottom-left at 11px.
- The errata slip stacks full width under the plate at −1°, so nothing overflows at 320px.
- Tapping the 'Specimen No. 02' label swaps its text to the chip text for 2s.
moves.perf_and_fallback: No runtime cost. Without JS, the label and the errata still render. Reduced motion: the stamp appears without the slam.

moves.name: Developer layer: console colophon, K2.help() and a live resize/refit readout
moves.where: Devtools console; window resize and phone rotation; the window.K2 namespace
moves.experience:
Opening devtools greets the developer jury with a printed colophon: a %c-styled block, IKB on paper, reading '4BOOSER Variable · Specimen No. 02 · wdth 50–150 · wght 100–900'.

It then invites play:
- K2.hero.strike(6)
- K2.strings.pluck(0,.5,1)
- K2.pigment.burst(innerWidth/2, innerHeight/2)
- K2.loud.setWord('HIRE ME')
- K2.help()

This is followed by a console.table of the scheduler's systems (name, active, last busy).

Resizing the window shows a mono readout bottom-right while you drag, for example '1440 × 900 → 1180 × 900 · refit 9 measures · 7 glyphs · 4 pins · 3.2 ms'. It fades 800ms after the last resize. Awwwards jurors resize everything; this tells them the fit engine is real.
moves.implementation:
- Log once after init with %c styles: colour, background, font-family, font-size and padding. Chrome and Safari honour them; Firefox ignores font-family, which is fine.
- K2.help() prints the API block that already exists as the section-1 comment, kept as a string.
- Wrap the existing layout() with performance.now() and counters, and return {measures, glyphs, pins, ms}.
- The .rsz element reuses the toast styles but is a separate aria-hidden node. It is updated from a scheduler tick only while resizing, and hides 800ms after the last resize.
moves.phone: Rotation shows the same readout ('390 × 844 → 844 × 390 · refit …'). The console is desktop-only by nature.
moves.perf_and_fallback: One log line at init, and work only during resizes. Nothing to fall back from.

moves.name: Selection inspector: design-tool spec chip on any selected text
moves.where: All selectable text: the h1, manifesto, case copy, email, footnotes and running heads
moves.experience:
Select any text and a chip appears above the selection, for example:
- 'ANYBODY 64/64 · W 80 · G 520 · 12 WORDS · 71 CHARS'
- 'ARCHIVO 16/24 · 2 LINES'

Selecting the email adds '@ copies it too'. Copying shows the toast 'Copied 71 characters — set in Anybody 64/64'. The clipboard is never modified.
moves.implementation:
- Listen to document 'selectionchange', debounced 80ms.
- Hide the chip if the selection is collapsed or inside an input or textarea.
- Otherwise call range.getBoundingClientRect() and getComputedStyle(startContainer.parentElement), once per change only. Read the first font-family token, size and leading (rounded), and parse font-variation-settings for wdth and wght.
- The chip is a fixed mono element (ink background, paper text, a 1px notch), clamped inside the viewport so it never causes horizontal overflow.
- Hide it when the scheduler sees F.dy ≠ 0, and re-show it on settle.
- The 'copy' event triggers the toast from sel.toString().length. Never call clipboardData.setData.
moves.phone: The OS selection handles and menu sit above the selection, so on coarse pointers the chip docks as a full-width strip at the bottom of the viewport, above the safe-area inset.
moves.perf_and_fallback: Event-driven, with no rAF. Reduced motion: no fade.

moves.name: Font-editor metrics: CAP / BASE reveal x-height, ascender, descender and overshoot
moves.where: Title page apparatus: the CAP and BASE labels in the right margin
moves.experience:
CAP and BASE become toggles. Hover, focus or tap draws the full metric stack across the name, like a font editor:
- ascender, cap height, x-height, baseline and descender lines;
- shaded overshoot bands (IKB 12%) where O and S round past the baseline and the cap line.

Each line gets a right-margin label in units per em, for example 'x 528 · cap 700 · desc −210 · overshoot 12'. The joke: the vertical metrics stay put while the advance boundaries keep moving with the string. In proof mode the metrics stay on.
moves.implementation:
- On each layout, measure once with an offscreen 2D canvas, using the existing cfont(100, 500, 1000) at 1000px.
- Take actualBoundingBoxAscent of 'x', 'H', 'O' and 'b', and actualBoundingBoxDescent of 'p' and 'O'. Convert to em units, then to px with the hero's current font-size (the fit engine already knows it).
- Add four 1px lines and two overshoot bands to the existing apparatus layer, next to the cap and baseline lines.
- A class toggle draws them with a 240ms scaleX from the left.
- Wrap CAP and BASE in <button aria-pressed>.
moves.phone: Tap CAP or BASE on either line (4BOO / SER). The lines draw across both lines.
moves.perf_and_fallback: One measure per layout and no per-frame work. Reduced motion: the lines appear without the draw.

moves.name: Live footnotes: hover text, jump with proof circle, exact return
moves.where: The footnote marks: * (FIG.1 caption), ‡ (Strings head), † (stats). The colophon footnote list. New § notes added by secrets.
moves.experience:
The marks become working references.
- **Hover or focus a mark:** the crop-mark rig wraps it, and its chip shows the note text (up to 42ch, two lines).
- **Click:** the page turns to the colophon and the folio flaps to 06. The note is circled with an IKB proof ellipse that draws in 500ms, and gains '↩ back to p.01', which returns to the exact scroll position you left.
- **Secrets append new notes live, with a flap-in:**
  - '§ Anybody has no Cyrillic. Sorts are on back order.'
  - '§ We don't talk about kerning.'
  - '§ You read the whole specimen. Thank you.'
moves.implementation:
- Wrap each sup.fn in <a class='fnref' href='#fn-N' aria-describedby='fn-N'>, and give ids to the generated <li>s in #fns.
- The Rig chip takes the note text from data-cursor-label. Allow two lines with max-width: 42ch.
- On click: store y0 = F.y, call K2.scrollTo(li, {focus: li}), add .ring (an SVG ellipse with stroke-dashoffset 1→0), and inject a back <a> that calls K2.scrollTo(y0) and then removes itself.
- New notes are added with K2.footnotes.push(...) followed by a render().
moves.phone: The first tap opens a small paper popover under the mark, with the note and 'Go to note →'. A second tap, or the link, jumps. The back link works the same way.
moves.perf_and_fallback: Event-driven. Without JS, the marks are plain in-page anchors that still jump.

moves.name: Title-page small parts: coin-flip seal stamp, local-time clock flip, speedometer monogram
moves.where: The No.02 seal; the hero '04 SET AT' clock and the colophon local time; the nav '4B' monogram
moves.experience:
**Seal**
- Hover flips it like a coin (rotateY 180°). The back face reads 'Proof · Est. 2020 · 4B'.
- Click stamps it. It presses (scale .9), and the paper takes a blind-embossed ring that fades over 4s.
- Each stamp sends a small pluck through all seven hero letters, as if the press shook the forme, plus a thud if sound is on.
- Five quick taps trigger the LOUD event.

**Clock**
Hover or tap flaps every digit from UTC to the visitor's own zone ('22:18:54 MSK'). Leaving flaps it back.

**Monogram**
- Hover swaps the instances of the 4 and the B: the 4 goes to 150/900, the B to 50/100.
- Scroll velocity stretches the B (wdth 100→150) like a speedometer, and it settles when you stop.
moves.implementation:
- **Seal:** two faces with backface-visibility hidden and a 600ms var(--ease-out) transition. On click, call Sound.thud(.5, .9) and a new K2.hero.nudge(amp), which adds a small velocity to all nodes. The .imp pseudo-element is a paper-on-paper emboss (1px light and dark offset shadows in a ring) that fades from opacity 1 to 0 over 4s. Count taps in a 1.5s window.
- **Clock:** add a mode flag. Format with Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, {hour, minute, second: '2-digit', hourCycle: 'h23', timeZoneName: 'short'}) and call flap() for each changed character.
- **Monogram:** wdth = 100 + min(50, |F.vel|/40). Write it in Chrome.tick only when the rounded value changes.
moves.phone: The seal and clock work by tap. The monogram reacts to native momentum scroll through F.vel.
moves.perf_and_fallback: Negligible: at most one fvs write when the rounded value changes. Reduced motion: the seal swaps faces by opacity, there is no emboss animation, and the monogram stays static.

moves.name: Key to the Specimen (?) and punctuation shortcuts
moves.where: A global keydown dispatcher; a '?' keycap in the nav (desktop, left of SOUND); a 'Key' row in the phone menu; Rig chips
moves.experience:
Shortcuts are punctuation that means its action:

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `?` | Key sheet |
| `#` | Proof marks |
| `!` | Sound (the loud key) |
| `.` | Drop a full stop of pigment at the cursor |
| `@` | Copy the email |
| `^` or `0` | Back to the title page |
| `1`–`6` | Turn to page 01–06 |
| `[` `]` | Previous / next page |
| `+` `−` | Turn the title page up / down |
| `<` `>` | Narrower / wider |
| `~` | Cycle brush tips |
| Esc | Close, clear or stop |

In a case: ← / → move to the previous or next plate, and 1–5 jump to a plate. Letters set type (move 18).

**The Key sheet** slides in from the right (520px wide; full screen on phones), titled 'Key to the Specimen'.
- Each row has a keycap (a 44px box, 1px ink border, 3px bottom border for depth) with its glyph set in Anybody. The rows ramp from 50/100 to 150/900 down the sheet, so the sheet is itself a specimen.
- Each row has dot leaders, the action, and live state (Sound ON, Proof OFF, Sorts 03/12).
- While the sheet is open, any key you press depresses its cap (translateY 2px, 90ms) and runs live, so the sheet doubles as a tester. Unknown keys show 'Last key: Ж · code Semicolon'.
- The footer lists the touch gestures and a 'Type to set: ON' switch: the off switch for character-key capture that WCAG 2.1.4 requires.

**Rig chips** stop repeating visible labels and teach keys instead: ESC over Close, ! over Sound, @ over Copy email, ^ over Rewind, 1–6 over the folio.
moves.implementation:
**Dispatcher**
- One document keydown listener, driven by a table: KEYS = [{key:'?', code:'Slash', shift:true, label, run, state}, …]. The sheet is rendered from the same table, so the docs cannot drift.
- Match e.key first, then fall back to e.code + shiftKey. A Russian layout has no '#' (Shift+3 gives '№'), so map it by code.
- Bail when:
  - the event is defaultPrevented or isComposing;
  - ctrl, meta or alt is held;
  - the target is an input, textarea, select or contenteditable;
  - the menu is open;
  - html.case-open is set (except for the case keys).
- Never preventDefault arrows or Space while the stick is empty.

**Key sheet**
role=dialog, aria-modal. Reuse focusables() and the menu's Tab trap. Set page.inert and call K2.lockScroll(true). Esc closes the sheet and restores focus.

**Actions**
- `.` calls K2.pigment.drop(P.inside ? P.x : vw/2, P.inside ? P.y : vh/2) plus Sound.thud. Over the band it toasts 'No pigment on blue'.
- `@` calls K2.copy. Keydown counts as user activation, so the clipboard works.
- `+` / `−` call K2.hero.setBias(0, ±100), clamped to ±300, with a toast such as 'Ramp +200'.
- `1`–`6` and `[` `]` call K2.scrollTo(Zones.folios[n].el, {duration: 1.2, focus}).
moves.phone: Phones have no hardware keys, so the menu gets a 'Key' row that opens the same sheet. It leads with the gestures (tap a letter to strike, swipe the name to pluck, long-press to charge, tap the seal 5×, Set a word) and keeps the keys for iPad keyboards. At 390px the sheet has 36px keycaps in one column and scrolls with data-lenis-prevent.
moves.perf_and_fallback: One listener, and the sheet is built on first open. Reduced motion: the sheet appears without the slide, and the caps don't animate. Without JS, the keys simply do nothing.

moves.name: Running-head print events: every section opens with a printed moment
moves.where: Every running head (4B—02 to 4B—06), the closing folios, and the threshold and instances heads
moves.implementation:
- One IntersectionObserver (rootMargin '0px 0px -12% 0px') on .rhead and .folio. Only heads below the fold at load are armed, so the no-JS state and first paint are the final state.
- CSS: .rhead::after is the overprint bar (var(--blue), transform-origin left). Its keyframes run scaleX 0→1, then opacity 1→0, over 700ms.
- .lead runs clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0)→inset(0), synced to the bar. The leaders are aria-hidden decoration.
- Digits use the existing flap().
- Sound: Sound.tick, plus a new Sound.zip() (noise through a bandpass swept 600→3kHz, 180ms, gated at 400ms).
- The Rewind run calls Heads.rearm().
moves.phone: Identical. It is cheap enough.
moves.perf_and_fallback: CSS animations and one IntersectionObserver, with no rAF. Reduced motion: disabled. Readable at rest: the rule, index and count are only overprinted. The leaders are the only thing withheld, for their 420ms draw.

moves.name: Book navigation: folio Contents popover and a dictionary thumb index
moves.where: The nav folio (desktop and phone); the right page edge (desktop, 1024px and wider)
moves.implementation:
- **Contents:** <div id='toc' role='menu'>. Use the popover attribute where supported, with a hidden-attribute fallback. Build it from Zones.folios on open. Items are real <a href='#id'> links routed through the existing anchor handler. Use a roving tabindex. Esc closes it and returns focus to the folio.
- **Flap-through:** step the folio number through the intermediate values with flap() every 70ms.
- **Thumb index:** a fixed <nav aria-label='Thumb index'> with six anchors. Tab heights come from Zones.folios in K2.onLayout. The mark's translateY is written in Chrome.tick only when it moves by more than 0.5px. Use mix-blend-mode difference in paper colour, so it reads on paper, ink and IKB.
moves.phone: Tapping the folio opens Contents full width under the nav, with 44px rows. There is no thumb index on phones, because the screen edge belongs to scroll gestures.
moves.perf_and_fallback: Negligible. Reduced motion: no flap-through and no slide. Without JS, the folio is plain text, and the anchors in the menu still work.

moves.name: Job case (12 secrets, visible and countable) and the hellbox
moves.where: Colophon left column, under Elsewhere / Availability / Local time (the empty IKB beside the plate on desktop); mirrored inside the Key sheet
moves.experience:
A California job case drawn in 1px paper lines on the IKB band. It has 12 compartments of different widths, like a real case.

**Unfound compartments** each show a hint as blank sorts:
- 'K _ _ _ _'
- '↑↑↓↓…'
- 'Sign as a master'
- 'Strike all seven'
- 'Open every plate'
- 'Type its name'
- 'Make it move'
- 'P _ _ _'
- 'Kern it'
- 'Say hello'
- 'Shh'
- 'Wrong family'

**Finding one:** a paper sort in Anybody 150/900 drops into its box with a flap and a rising two-note sound. A toast reads 'Sort 05/12 — KERN'. The header reads 'Job case — 05/12 sorts'.

**Hellbox:** beside the case, 'Hellbox · 17 sorts' counts every piece of discarded type: backspaced sorts, letters knocked off LOUD, and swapped-out MAKE ___ LOUD words. 'Distribute' empties it with a tick cascade.

**12/12:** adds a § footnote and 'Complete set' to the plate caption.
moves.phone: The case is 3 × 4 compartments, full width under the contact block. Hints are 11px mono. The unlock toasts are the same.
moves.perf_and_fallback: Static DOM. Reduced motion: sorts appear without the drop. Without storage, the case resets on each visit.

moves.name: Instrument mode everywhere: the index is a xylophone, plus a 7-string VU meter
moves.where: Global sound map; the nav SOUND indicator; the phone MENU button
moves.experience:
With SOUND ON, the whole page is tuned to the hero's pentatonic set (A2 C3 D3 E3 G3 A3 C4):
- **Work index:** running the cursor down it plays an ascending scale (row n plays note n+1, an octave up, soft).
- **Nav links:** each plucks its own note.
- **Running heads:** zip as they print.
- **Stick sorts:** clack at the pitch of their position, so every typed word has a tune. Enter strums the word and rings a carriage-return bell.
- **Footnote jumps:** play a paper turn.
- **Job-case unlocks:** a rising two-note.
- **Proof mode:** toggles with a lamp click.

The 'SOUND ○' indicator becomes a 7-bar mono VU meter. Each bar (1px wide, 9px tall) is one string: it jumps when that string sounds and decays in 300ms. You can see the instrument even on a muted device.
moves.phone: The same sounds play on taps. The VU meter replaces the dot in the menu's sound row, and appears as a small glyph beside MENU while sound is on.
moves.perf_and_fallback: Negligible: rate-limited and voice-capped, and nothing exists until the AudioContext is created on the toggle. Reduced motion: the VU meter shows state without bouncing. Sound itself is unchanged.

moves.name: Plate upgrades: paint on the plate, hold-to-replay time-lapse, PAPER / BLACK / LEAF stock
moves.where: The Anthropometry plate (colophon)
moves.experience:
**(a) Paint on the plate.** Drag on the paper and the strokes go straight into your print. They are logged like page strokes, so the caption counts them. This also fixes the empty state.

**(b) Hold to replay.** Press and hold, and your visit redraws as a 3s time-lapse in the order you painted, with a moving pigment head and the duration counter rolling.

**(c) Stock.**
- PAPER: the current print.
- BLACK: your strokes print as Monogold on black (Klein's gold).
- LEAF: IKB on gold leaf with faint leaf seams.

**(d) The plate also shows:**
- words printed from the stick, as set words;
- found sorts, as tiny registration marks in the margin;
- the FORGERY stamp (move 1).
moves.implementation:
- Ant.print() gains (stock, tEnd) parameters, with a ground fill and stroke colour per stock:
  - paper: #E6E7E3 / IKB;
  - black: #0E0E10 / #D4AF37;
  - leaf: #D4AF37 / IKB, with 12 seeded polygon seams at 4% ink.
  Gold here is the plate's material, the same family as the seal.
- **Replay:** a scheduler system advances tEnd over 3s and draws only the stroke segments between the previous tEnd and the new one. Strokes are already time-stamped in the log, so there is no full redraw per frame.
- **Direct paint:** pointer events on the plate canvas, with touch-action: none on the canvas only. Points are mapped back to document coordinates through the inverse of the plate mapping.
- **Stock control:** a 3-way segmented control with aria-pressed.
moves.phone: The plate is full width, with the stock control under the caption. Replay starts on long-press (contextmenu is suppressed on the canvas only). Painting on the plate works with a finger.
moves.perf_and_fallback: Redraws happen only on demand, and replay lasts 3s. Reduced motion: replay jumps straight to the final print. Painting still works because it is direct manipulation.

moves.name: Proof mode (#): grid, live spec tags, proofreader's marks and scheduler telemetry
moves.where: A global overlay. Opened with the # key, a nav keycap, or 'Proof marks' in the phone menu.
moves.implementation:
- **Overlay:** one absolutely positioned layer inside .page. It scrolls natively, is clipped by overflow-x: clip, has pointer-events: none, and sits just under the pigment.
- **Grid and baseline:** repeating-linear-gradients, with no DOM.
- **Static tags:** elements opt in with data-spec. They are measured once on toggle and again in K2.onLayout, in the read phase only.
- **Animated tags:** systems register getters with K2.spec.watch(el, () => [size, w, g]):
  - Hero, from its wd/wg arrays;
  - Strings;
  - Board;
  - Loud.
  A ProofSys scheduler entry is active only while proof mode is on. It throttles to 15 Hz and writes textContent only when a rounded value changes.
- **Telemetry:** the scheduler fills a reusable busyNames array in frame() (one line) and keeps an EMA of dt. Written at 4 Hz.
- **Marks:** a static array of {selector, text, side}, positioned from cached rects.
moves.phone:
Opened from the menu.
- The grid has 4 columns.
- Tags are limited to section boxes, hero letters and the board.
- Marks are hidden, because there are no margins.
- Telemetry is one 9px line above the bottom safe area.
moves.perf_and_fallback: No cost while off. While on: about 40 positioned tags, text writes at no more than 15 Hz, and one extra busy system. Reduced motion: no flicker. Without JS, nothing changes.

moves.name: Instances: fidget flaps, designspace probe, and a waterfall in the dead middle
moves.where: The Instances board (pinned, on ink), the designspace plot, and the empty middle cell between the stage copy and the plot (desktop)
moves.experience:

moves.experience:

- **Double-click (double-tap) a word:** it strikes like a hero letter. It punches to wght 900, springs back with overshoot, and plucks if sound is on. The same verb everywhere.

moves.implementation:
- The words are already spans for the ink-up; add data-i.
- **Strike:** the Text system animates the word's weight for 600ms. To stop the pre-broken line from reflowing, measure the punched width once on dblclick and apply transform: scaleX(natural / punched) during the punch.
- **'move,' repel:** in Text.tick when the pointer is within 120px. Its rect is cached in layout. Write a transform only.

moves.name: Scrubbable hero readouts and hold-to-charge strike
moves.where: Title page: the W/G readouts under each letter, and the letters themselves
moves.experience:
**Readouts** behave like number fields in a design tool.
- Hover 'W 061': crop marks wrap it with a '⟷ SCRUB' chip.
- Drag sideways to set that letter's rest width (50–150). Drag on 'G 189' to set its weight (100–900).
- The letter and its micro-bars follow live, the measure stays fitted, and the string stays live, so plucks ride on top of your custom ramp.
- Shift-drag moves in steps of 10. Double-click resets the letter. The FIG.1 caption then reads 'RAMP · CUSTOM · ⟲ reset'.

**Holding a letter charges it.**
- wght climbs toward 900 over 800ms, the letter squashes and leans back, and the crop marks tighten.
- A rising tremolo plays if sound is on.
- On release, the strike is scaled by the charge: a bigger pigment burst and a harder kick through the chain.
- A quick tap is still the existing strike.
moves.implementation:
**Hero API**
- Add restW and restG as Float32Array(7) filled with NaN (NaN means 'use the ramp'). Read them wherever the rest ramp is computed.
- Add setBias(dw, dg) and setRamp({w0, w1, g0, g1}, ms), which moves 7 and 17 also use.

**Readouts**
- role='slider', tabindex 0, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuenow, and an aria-label such as 'Letter 3 width'.
- ← / → step by 1, Shift by 10; Home and End jump to the limits.
- Pointer capture on pointerdown; Δx × 0.5 becomes the value. Hero writes the new value on its next tick, so there is no layout read after a write.

**Charge**
- A 180ms hold threshold.
- Past it, Hero.charge[i] grows by dt/0.8, and pigment injection under that pointer is paused.
- On pointerup: strike(i, x, y, 1 + 2·charge). strike gains a strength argument that scales the burst and the kick.

Rewind clears all overrides.
moves.phone:
- Readout hit areas are padded to 44px tall.
- touch-action: none goes on the readouts only. They are small targets, so page scroll is unaffected.
- Long-pressing a letter charges it. The name already has pan-y, and a still finger does not cancel the gesture.
- The letter spans get -webkit-touch-callout: none and user-select: none. The h1 text stays accessible.
moves.perf_and_fallback: No new loops; the Hero system already runs. Reduced motion: scrubbing still works (direct manipulation), the charge is a static weight change, and the strike has no burst.

moves.name: LOUD event (Konami ↑↑↓↓←→←→BA, typing LOUD, or tapping the seal 5×) and its inverse, WHISPER
moves.where: Global, centred on the title page, the strings and sound
moves.experience:
**LOUD**
- A rubber stamp 'LOUD' slams onto the centre of the viewport with a thud and a three-hit screen shake (4px, decaying). The stamp is Anybody 150/900 with a 3px IKB outline, rotated −8° like the seal.
- The title page's ramp flattens to Black Extended 150/900 for 10s. The fit engine shrinks the type to hold the measure, so LOUD visibly makes the name smaller and blacker: a type joke worth a footnote.
- Both strings are plucked hard, and the nav reads 'SOUND ● LOUD'.
- With sound on, a 55Hz sine swell lands under all seven strings struck as a chord, and the low-pass opens fully.
- With sound off, the stamp's subline says 'Press ! for the full set'.

**WHISPER**
The inverse:
- the ramp goes to 50/100;
- a hairline stamp reads 'whisper';
- the master gain drops 12dB for 6s;
- the rig shrinks to 12px marks.
moves.implementation:
- **Konami:** a rolling buffer of the last 10 e.key values in the dispatcher. The arrows still scroll normally. On a match, the B and A sorts are removed from the stick.
- **Ramp:** Hero.setRamp({w0: 150, w1: 150, g0: 900, g1: 900}, 10000). The chain's spring eases to the new rest, then restores it.
- **Strings:** K2.strings.pluck(0, .3, 1) and pluck(1, .7, 1).
- **Shake:** a WAAPI translate on .page, three keyframe hits, transform only. Skipped under env.reduce.
- **Sound:** Sound.bass() is a 55Hz sine with a gain envelope 0→.5→0 over 1.2s. The chord is ks[0..6] strummed at a 25ms stagger, and Sound.lp.frequency.setTargetAtTime(12000).
- **Stamp:** a fixed element with keyframes (scale 1.8→1, then fade at 2.4s).
- **Secrets:** K2.secrets.unlock('loud'), unlock('konami') or unlock('whisper').
moves.phone: Type LOUD or WHISPER in the stick (menu → 'Set a word'), or tap the No.02 seal 5 times within 1.5s.
moves.perf_and_fallback: Uses systems that are already running: 10s of hero activity. Reduced motion: no shake and no slam (the stamp fades in and out), and the ramp jumps instead of easing.

moves.name: Composing stick: type anywhere, Enter prints your word in Klein pigment (plus 12 magic words)
moves.where: Global, fixed bottom-centre above the safe area. On phones, via 'Set a word' in the menu.
moves.experience:
**The stick**
Type any letter with nothing focused, and a composing stick slides up from the bottom edge: a 1px ink rail labelled 'STICK · 05 SORTS · ↵ PRINT · ESC DISTRIBUTE'.
- **Letters:** each drops in as a sort, 56px, set in Anybody. The sorts ramp left to right from 50/100 to 150/900 like the title page, so your word is set as a specimen. Each sort clacks at its own pentatonic pitch, so every word has a tune.
- **Backspace:** pulls the last sort out, and it hops into the hellbox.
- **Space:** a word space.

**Enter locks up and prints**
- The stick squashes like a platen hitting the forme, with a thud.
- Your word prints onto the page in Klein pigment, fitted to about 70% of the viewport at 150/900 and centred on the cursor.
- It blooms into tendrils, dries to halftone and dissolves like every stroke.
- It is logged to the Anthropometry plate as a set word.

**Cyrillic layouts**
Anybody has no Cyrillic (verified: Google Fonts ships only latin, latin-ext and vietnamese). So the sort shows a .notdef tofu box labelled NOTDEF for 600ms, then transliterates to the Latin key under your finger. A § footnote appears: 'Anybody has no Cyrillic. Sorts are on back order.'

**Magic words** (matched by physical key, so any layout works)
- **KLEIN** or **IKB:** floods the viewport with pigment from the centre (paper → IKB, ink → gold), with the toast 'International Klein Blue — Yves Klein, 1960'.
- **GOLD:** switches the pigment to Monogold leaf for 20s (paper → gold, ink → deep blue).
- **LOUD** and **WHISPER:** move 17.
- **MOVE:** every 'move' on the page moves: the hero's 'move.', the manifesto's 'move,' and 'Moves'.
- **BOOSER:** a roll call of seven strikes left to right, with an ascending pentatonic run.
- **PLAY:** turns the title page into a 7-step sequencer for 4 bars at 112 BPM, with a 1px IKB playhead. It needs sound on, and any input stops it.
- **KERN:** crashes the sorts together, and the label reads 'KEMING'.
- **COMIC** or **PAPYRUS:** turns the sorts to tofu, with 'Not an instance of this family.'
- **HELLO:** copies the email with a ripple.

Each found word flashes IKB, gets a 'FOUND' stamp, and drops a sort into the job case.
moves.implementation:
**Dispatcher fallthrough**
- Letters come from /^[a-z]$/i on e.key; otherwise e.code KeyA–KeyZ gives the letter (the Cyrillic path).
- At most 14 sorts. Past that, a jam shake and 'Stick full'.
- Space and Backspace are preventDefault'ed only while the stick is non-empty.
- The stick takes Enter only when focus is on the body or the stick, so a focused button keeps its native Enter.

**Stick DOM**
A fixed <div role='status' aria-live='polite'> holding sort spans. translateY(110%) while empty. Stacked above the pigment and below the case sheet.

**Print primitive**
One new pigment program, 'stamp':
- dye += texture(uMask, maskUV).a × amt inside uRect;
- plus a velocity pass that adds an outward push × mask, so the word blooms.
The mask is a 512×128 2D canvas drawn with the existing cfont(150, 900, px) and uploaded with texImage2D: one draw per print.

**Ship-first fallback** (also the '2d' mode path)
Sample about 180 alpha points from the same mask with one getImageData, and K2.pigment.splat them left to right over 300ms, like a roller pass.

**Logging**
Push {k: 'word', text, x, docY, w} for Ant.print().

**GOLD**
Lerp PIG.X toward PIG.XB over 600ms, and back after 20s. PIG.XB already maps paper to #D4AF37 Monogold, and ink becomes #042A9C. X is uploaded every display frame, so no shader change is needed.

**KLEIN**
Three radial stamps of growing radius over 500ms, from a radial-gradient mask.

**Words**
A table of {word, run, secret}.
moves.phone:
There is no global typing on touch.
- The menu row 'Set a word' opens the stick with a real <input> (enterkeyhint='done', autocapitalize='characters'). Its value mirrors into sorts.
- The stick rides above the on-screen keyboard using visualViewport (offsetTop + height).
- Enter prints at the centre of the screen.
- Magic words work the same.
moves.perf_and_fallback:
DOM exists only while the stick is open. Each print is one GL draw, or 180 splats over 300ms on the fallback.

Reduced motion (pigment off): Enter prints the word straight onto the plate, with the toast 'Printed to your plate'. Magic words run their non-motion parts.

WCAG 2.1.4: the 'Type to set' switch in the Key sheet turns character-key capture off.

moves.name: Idle autopilot: the specimen sets itself
moves.where: Desktop with a fine pointer; plays the section currently on screen
moves.experience:
After 20s with no input (tab visible, pointer inside), a second crop-mark rig glides in. It is outlined in ink at 40%, with the chip 'AUTOPILOT · move to take over'. It performs the section on screen for up to 6s, then rests for 8s.

| Section | What the ghost does |
|---|---|
| Title | Sweeps across the name, strikes the R, paints a short stroke under 'move.' |
| Strings | One sweep across a tape |
| Text | Paints along the reading line |
| In Use | Strolls down the index so the riso cards show; never opens one |
| Instances | Taps a tile (fidget) |
| Colophon | Nudges a LOUD letter and drops a full stop |

After 3 performances it stops until the next real input. Any input ends it at once, and the ghost fades out in 200ms. It makes the page perform for anyone who leaves it open, and it teaches the gestures.
moves.phone: Off, because phones have no idle cursor. The hero's slow breath remains the only autonomous motion.
moves.perf_and_fallback: Runs only while idle, and costs only what the triggered systems cost. Reduced motion: off.

moves.name: Brush tips: ROUND · CHISEL · TYPE (the glyph-trail idea, done in pigment)
moves.where: The FIG.2 caption in Text setting becomes the brush selector; the ~ key; the phone menu
moves.experience:
The FIG.2 caption becomes a live control and readout: 'FIG.2 KLEIN PIGMENT · BRUSH ROUND / CHISEL / TYPE · 12 strokes · 3 drops'.
- **CHISEL:** a broad nib held at 30°. Horizontal strokes are hairlines and diagonals are fat, so a scribble reads as brush lettering.
- **TYPE:** writes 4-B-O-O-S-E-R along your stroke as pigment stamps (Anybody 150/900, turned to the direction of travel, sized by speed). The visitor literally signs the name in Klein blue.

The ~ key cycles tips from anywhere.
moves.implementation:
- **CHISEL:** no GL change. For each sample, place two splats offset ±n × the nib vector, with radius scaled by |sin(angle − 30°)|.
- **TYPE:** uses the stamp program from move 18 with a 7-cell glyph atlas (one 2D canvas, 7 × 128px cells, cfont(150, 900)) and a per-stamp uRect and rotation. One stamp per 70px of travel, at most 15 per second.
- **2D fallback:** fillText the glyphs on the fallback canvas with the blot fade.
- The chosen tip is a per-viewer convenience, saved in localStorage inside try/catch.
moves.phone: Tap the caption options. TYPE stamps along finger strokes, using the same atlas at half resolution.
moves.perf_and_fallback: CHISEL doubles the splat count, still capped by the existing QMAX. TYPE adds at most 15 draws per second. Reduced motion: pigment is off, so the selector is hidden.

moves.name: Strings as an index: skills cross-reference the plates
moves.where: The skill words on both tapes, linked to the In Use rows
moves.experience:
Each skill on the tapes is an index entry.
- **Hover TYPESCRIPT:** the chip reads 'TYPESCRIPT → plates 01 · 03 · 05'.
- **Click:** the page turns to In Use. The matching rows get an IKB underline sweep, and their 'Plate 0n →' flashes for 2.5s ('see also').

Clicking an entry also plucks the tape at that word.

- A click counts only if the pointer travelled less than 5px, so the tape-scrub drag keeps working.
- Work.highlight(ids, ms) adds a class: a CSS background-size sweep on the title underline.

reject:
**NIGHT PRESS global retheme: reject.**
- The contract is a single deliberate light look.
- The threshold (paper to an ink O) and the flood (ink to IKB) seams depend on the paper/ink order.
- The riso plates print ink #0E0E10, which disappears on black stock.
- The pigment's difference colour X is tuned for paper (3.9:1).
- It doubles QA for every screenshot.

Making it the default for prefers-color-scheme: dark would silently replace the designed identity. Its best idea, Klein's gold on black, lives on the plate's BLACK stock and in the GOLD word.

**LETTERPRESS PLATEN as a transition between sections: reject.** A full-viewport press at every boundary hijacks reading, and the page already has two set-piece transitions (the threshold zoom and the flood). Use the platen once, at small scale, as the stick's Enter lock-up. The paper sections get running-head print events instead.

**Single-letter shortcuts (G for grid, N for night, and so on): reject.**
- They collide with type-anywhere and the magic words: G is in GOLD, N in KLEIN.
- They would need a WCAG 2.1.4 off switch anyway.
- They break on non-Latin layouts.

Punctuation keys carry meaning and don't collide.
**HERO SEQUENCER as default sound-on behaviour: reject.** Someone who turns sound on for plucks would get an unrequested loop. Keep it as the PLAY magic word, with a hard stop on any input.
**CURSOR GLYPH TRAIL as a separate follower: reject.** A third cursor follower, after the rig and the pigment brush, is noise. The idea becomes the TYPE brush tip, which writes 4BOOSER in pigment.

**Velocity-based global type stretch while scrolling: reject.** The hero and the strings already respond to scroll velocity. Stretching all text would reflow paragraphs mid-scroll (layout thrash) and hurt readability. Velocity goes only to the nav monogram and the proof-mode telemetry.

**Konami 'everything to 150/900': reject the 'everything'.** It has the same reflow and overflow problem as the mixer. LOUD becomes an event on the title page, the strings and the sound, with a screen shake.
**Full-screen screensaver takeover: reject.** Keep the in-place autopilot, which plays only the section on screen, stops on the first input, and retires after 3 performances.

**Page-wide wipes between every section: reject.** Six set pieces in a row would turn reading into waiting. The existing title flight, threshold and flood stay as the big moves, and the rest get cheap running-head print events.

**Print stylesheet and document.title or favicon tricks (my own candidates): reject.** In the claude.ai artifact frame, Ctrl+P prints the host page with the iframe clipped, and the host owns the tab title and icon. None of it would be seen.
**Hellbox as a separate hidden place: merged** into the job case as a live counter with a Distribute action. A separate destination would be one more thing to find, with nothing in it.

thesis:
ONE PRESS, ONE VOLUME KNOB. The page already has a real dramatic arc: a whisper hero, a quiet text section, the zoom drop, a rising board, the flood, and the LOUD peak. "Maximum" should not mean piling more effects side by side. It should mean four things. (1) The crescendo becomes a global, visible, controllable quantity (VOL 0–10, plus 11). (2) The page can show its own working (PROOF). (3) Every seam between sections becomes a cue on one director timeline. (4) The visit gets a real ending that loops: press pull, then a tape rewind that replays the visitor's own strokes, then calibration, then the seal stamp.

Rules for every addition: it is a print or press operation; it has a mono readout; it settles back to a readable specimen page within seconds (or is an explicit opt-in mode); and it can be reached by click or tap. The artifact iframe only receives keys after it has focus, so a keyboard route can never be the only route.

SHARED ARCHITECTURE (build first):
- K2.mode {vol 0–11, proof, stock, leaf, show}, mirrored to html attributes and CSS variables, plus a 'k2:mode' event.
- K2.director: one page-scale event at a time. Priority: rewind > press-pull > KLEIN / ELEVEN > snap > demonstration. The demonstration never starts within 6s of another event. Downbeats run reversed while rewinding.
- No second WebGL context and no new library is needed. The PROOF quiver and GOLD leaf are branches in the existing pigment display shader. Everything else is 2D canvas, CSS or WebAudio.

PROPOSED STAGE SPLIT:
- Stage D, modes and controls: mode bus + director, PROOF, VOLUME (console and 11), composing stick (KLEIN, GOLD, hellbox), and NIGHT behind a flag only if time allows.
- Stage E, direction: lock-ups and downbeats on every seam, typographic flood, threshold loupe, string snap, demonstration with sequencer, press pull ending, rewind replay, pull-to-rewind lever, and the LOUD full stop docking into the email (hand-off from stage C).
- If only one big-ticket item gets built, build VOLUME: it is the thesis made interactive. It has the highest risk, so give it most of stage D.

UPGRADED BEAT SHEET (phone differences in the moves):
- B0 Calibration, 0–1.6s: ruler, reels and ghost brush as now. New at 1.45s: the No.02 seal stamps down (scale 1.3→1, −16°→−8°, thud) and the nav level meter sweeps up to 05, meaning "set at spec volume".
- B1 Title (4B—01): pluck and strike. After 16s idle, demonstration act 1: the ghost rig sweeps the name, strikes R and then 4, and paints in the margin. With sound on, this is a seeded 7-step riff.
- Seam 1→2: the 4B—02 running head locks up (rule draws with ruler ticks, index flaps 00→02, leaders run, count rolls 00→10). Its downbeat plucks both tapes.
- B2 Strings: ring with scroll. New peak: a hard flick snaps a tape at the crossing; the halves whip and dangle, then it is re-strung in 2.4s with tuning ticks.
- Seam 2→3: the 4B—03 lock-up mutes the strings (the band stops for the verse).
- B3 Text: the calm valley, untouched. The demonstration never acts here.
- Seam 3→4: the 4B—04 downbeat kiss-prints the five rows from the top down: blind deboss, then ink lands with a short wght squash, then an IKB ghost settles into register. One thud per row.
- B4 In Use: riso card, title flight, KINETIK case as now. Demonstration act: the rig walks rows 01→05, so an idle visitor sees every plate.
- Seam 4→5: the card is hidden, HOW A PROJECT types on at 50/100, and the master low-pass closes (an inhale before the drop).
- B5 Threshold: the zoom into the O, with a live loupe readout ×01.0→×70.0, crop marks closing in on the zoom point, the paper grain growing, and a sub-bass drop at 90%.
- B6 Instances: the split-flap board as now.
- B7 Flood, now typographic: every flap spills a glyph that steps from 50/100 to 150/900 before landing as blank IKB, with a tick cascade rising in pitch.
- B8 Colophon LOUD (stage C): the letters drop. The rolling full stop docks as the dot of .dev and fires the email's ripple. MAKE ___ LOUD also accepts commands. Demonstration act: the chips cycle NOISE, WAVES, HISTORY.
- B9 Coda, PRESS PULL: a platen rolls down the Anthropometry plate and prints the visit as a score. The same No.02 seal stamps it "1/1", closing the bookend from B0. Imprint line: "End of Specimen No. 02 — pulled 19:22:04 UTC".
- B10 Loop, REWIND (click it, or keep pulling past the bottom): the folio flaps 06→01, the meter drains, seams retract, and the visitor's own strokes replay backwards at their document positions, un-painting upward. A descending pentatonic plays. Calibration replays and the seal re-stamps. The visit ends where it began.
- Modes can overlay any beat: VOL 0–10 (whisper to LOUD; 11 = LOUD MODE), PROOF, KLEIN, GOLD, and optionally NIGHT.

PERFORMANCE BUDGET: at rest, the new systems add zero rAF work. PROOF redraws only on scroll or busy frames. VOL runs one batched fit read per frame, and only while it is moving. The demonstration runs only when idle, for at most 45s. The replay runs only during the rewind.
