moves.name: Running-head lock-ups + section downbeats (every seam is a cue)
moves.where: All six .rhead running heads and the seams 1→2, 2→3, 3→4, 4→5, on K2.director. The threshold zoom and the flood stay the only full-screen transitions.
moves.experience:
As each section's running head crosses about 82% of the viewport, it locks up like a forme being tightened:
- the 1px rule draws left to right, with B0's ruler ticks flickering along it;
- the index flaps 4B—00 → 4B—0n;
- the dot leaders run out from the title;
- the right-hand count rolls (00→10 STYLES, 00→57 WORDS, 00→05 PLATES).

On the last frame, that section's own system gets a downbeat:
- 4B—02: both tapes are plucked.
- 4B—03: the strings are muted (silence before the verse).
- 4B—04: the five rows kiss-print from the top down: blind deboss, then ink lands with a 2-frame +120 wght squash, then an IKB ghost 2px out of register settles. One thud per row.
- Threshold: HOW A PROJECT types on at 50/100 and the low-pass closes.
- Board: every tile flaps once.
- Band: the LOUD drop (stage C).

Scrolling up retracts each lock-up right to left, so REWIND plays every seam backwards for free.
moves.implementation:
- Director.seams = [{rh, docTop, armed, down()}]. docTop is cached in layout() the same way Zones does it; the frame loop does no rect reads.
- Read phase: p = smoothstep over a 120px band around 0.82·vh, from (docTop − scrollY). Write --lk on the rhead.
- CSS: rule transform scaleX(var(--lk)) with origin left; leaders via background-size; the title is revealed with clip-path inset. All scroll-scrubbed and reversible.
- When p crosses .5 in either direction, call flap() on the index and roll the count (rAF tween, tabular figures, Sound.tick per step).
- The downbeat fires once per downward pass, when p reaches 1 and F.vel > 0. It re-arms when p < .2. It is suppressed while a case or the menu is open or the director is busy.
- Row kiss: add .kiss with a 70ms stagger. Keyframes go from a paper/ink-8% inset text-shadow (blind) to ink plus wght +120 and back. An ::after IKB copy translates (2px, 1px), opacity .5 → 0, over 320ms. Sound.thud(rowX, .4).
- The default CSS state is fully locked. JS adds .pre only to sections that are below the fold at load.
moves.phone: Same mechanism with an 80px band and 450ms timings. The counts roll in tabular figures. The kiss-print runs per row, without the card. Thuds are panned by row centre (mostly mono on a phone).
moves.perf_and_fallback:
- Cost is about 0.1ms per frame: transforms, background-size and clip only, with no layout reads.
- No-JS and reduced motion: running heads are static and fully drawn, and downbeats are skipped.
- Labels never fade; only the rule and leaders scrub. A still at any scroll position stays readable.

moves.name: PROOF mode: the specimen shows its working
moves.where:
- Nav button 'PROOF ⊞' next to SOUND on desktop.
- Key G, and the composing-stick words GRID / PROOF.
- Phone: a toggle in the menu.
- One fixed 2D overlay canvas, z between pigment (70) and grain (75), pointer-events none.
moves.implementation:
- Proof system, active when K2.mode.proof is on.
- Static layer: on layout, collect [data-proof] elements (hero .k, .rhead, row titles, thr words, tiles, loud lines, email, manifesto lines). Store doc rects plus fvs and font-size read once.
- Redraw only when F.dy ≠ 0, after layout, or while a live system is busy. Pick the line colour per element with Zones.toneAt: IKB 55% on paper, paper 40% on ink or IKB.
- Live layer: K2.proof.hooks, one draw(ctx) per system, called only when proof is on and the system is active. Sources:
  - Hero: its node arrays.
  - Strings: sample points.
  - Phys: Matter.Composite.allBodies() vertices plus constraints.
  - Board: hinge y per tile.
- Pigment: add uProof and a velocity sampler to the display program. Per 24px cell, sample v at the cell centre and draw a 1px segment of length min(|v|·k, 20px) where |v| > ε. That is one extra fetch per pixel, and proof never keeps the sim awake.
- HUD: the scheduler wraps each tick in performance.now() only while proof is on; the text updates at 4Hz.
- Mode is kept in sessionStorage (try/catch).
moves.phone:
- Menu toggle 'Proof'.
- 4-column grid, baselines and display boxes only.
- Per-word chips appear only on tap: tapping a display word in proof mode pins its chip for 3s.
- The HUD collapses to one mono line above the safe area.
- No quiver below a DPR budget.
moves.perf_and_fallback:
- Off: zero cost (system inactive, canvas display:none).
- On: about 0.3–0.8ms per scrolled frame (≤300 segments), plus one texture fetch in the pigment display pass.
- Without WebGL the quiver is omitted; without Matter the hulls are omitted.
- Reduced motion: no plotter pass, an instant static draw.

moves.name: REWIND as tape replay: your visit un-paints itself
moves.where: Rewind.run (foot bar), the Pigment strokes log, Chrome's folio flap and the Sound engine.
moves.experience:
PLAY IT AGAIN now replays the visit backwards.
- The letters kick.
- During the 2.4s scroll to the top, the folio flaps 06→05→…→01 and the level meter drains.
- The scrubbed systems and seam lock-ups run backwards, which they already do for free.
- The money shot: every pigment stroke the visitor painted reappears at its exact document position as the page passes it, and is drawn backwards (newest first, brush travelling in reverse). The visitor watches their own visit un-paint itself on the way up.
- Sound: a descending pentatonic arpeggio of the seven hero notes, one per folio change, over a tape-wind whoosh.
- At the top, calibration replays and the seal re-stamps.
moves.implementation:
- A Replay system is active only while Rewind is running.
- At start, set cursor = Pigment.ln − 1.
- Each frame, walk the log backwards from the cursor while entries lie within ±0.6vh of the current viewport band (document px). For each entry:
  - strokes (kind 0): K2.pigment.splat(x·vw, docY − scrollY, −dx, −dy, {ghost:true, dye:.8}), where dx and dy are the delta to the previous point of the same sid;
  - blots: drop({ghost:true}).
- Cap at 40 splats per frame (QMAX is 160) and skip entries the band has already passed.
- Ghost splats are not logged, so the plate keeps the original.
- Chrome already flaps on folio change; call Sound.pluck(6 − n, .5) on each change.
- If the log is empty, replay the intro ghost path reversed.
moves.phone: Identical, through the native ScrollTween path. Multi-touch strokes replay as separate sids.
moves.perf_and_fallback:
- Splats are queue pushes, and the sim is awake during the rewind anyway.
- The 2D blot fallback replays blots.
- Pigment off or reduced motion: the instant jump stays as now, with no replay.

moves.name: PRESS PULL: the ending prints your visit
moves.where: The Anthropometry plate in the colophon, the No.02 seal, the foot imprint line, and the recomposed band spread (the desktop dead zone).
moves.experience:
When the plate first reaches about 55% in view, and again whenever there is new pigment since the last pull, the visit is printed:
- A platen (ink bar across the sheet, 14% of its height, with a 1px brayer highlight) rolls down the sheet in 900ms.
- Behind it, the visitor's marks print with ink spread (radius ×1.25 → 1, slight bleed), and the IKB plate settles from 2px to 0.5px out of register.
- The plate is now a score of the visit: strokes and drops, hero strikes as radial ticks, plucks as tiny waveform marks in the left margin at their section's height, and flung LOUD letters as impact dots, all against the section ticks 01–06.
- The No.02 gold seal then stamps the corner with a thud. It is the same 56px / −8° object as on the title page, so the only gold element opens and closes the specimen.
- The edition line sets: 'ANT 4B–8326 · edition 1/1 · pulled 19:22:04 UTC'.
- The foot reads 'End of Specimen No. 02'.

The empty state still prints: its message is blind-debossed, and the seal stamps 'Unpainted proof'.
moves.implementation:
- New log kinds: 2 strike (Hero.strike), 3 pluck (Hero/Strings at |amp| > τ, gated to 4/s), 4 fling (Phys impact > threshold).
- Ant.print(q) gets a reveal parameter: clip y ≤ q·h, plus a per-mark spread factor from its distance to the platen line. The platen is drawn on the same canvas.
- The seal is a DOM clone of .seal with a CSS stamp keyframe (scale 1.35→1, rotate −16→−8, 220ms, cubic-bezier(.2,1.6,.4,1)), plus Sound.thud.
- The pull time comes from Clock.
- Director priority 2.
- Recompose the band: the plate column spans the contact block; the empty area takes the credits table and the hellbox count.
moves.phone: The plate is full width, the platen takes 700ms, the seal is 44px, and the credits stack under the plate.
moves.perf_and_fallback:
- One 2D redraw per frame for 0.9s, then idle.
- Reduced motion: the final printed state, with the seal already stamped.
- If the canvas fails, the DOM empty state and the seal still render.

moves.name: COMPOSING STICK: type words, the press obeys (KLEIN, GOLD, hellbox)
moves.where:
- A global keydown listener that ignores inputs, modifier keys and open dialogs.
- A fixed stick at bottom-left.
- The MAKE ___ LOUD input, which is the route on every device.
- A new footnote §.
- A hellbox counter in the colophon.
moves.experience:
Letters typed anywhere land as metal sorts in a composing stick: boxed mono glyphs, mirrored like real type. When the stick spells a word the press knows, the sorts flip to right-reading (flap) and the word fires:
- KLEIN: the pigment floods the viewport in 600ms into an IKB monochrome with gold type for about 2.5s (toast 'IKB · after Yves Klein'), then dries into halftone.
- GOLD: the brush switches to Monogold leaf. Paper prints #D4AF37, type prints navy, and drying edges crack into leaf squares. It lasts until KLEIN or BLUE.
- GRID / PROOF: proof mode.
- LOUD / ELEVEN (and the Konami code as an alias): VOL 11.
- WHISPER: VOL 0.
- SHOW: starts the demonstration.
- NIGHT / DAY: night press.
- 4BOOSER: the string plays the name as a phrase with a strike cascade.
- REWIND: the rewind.

Unknown words tip off the stick after 1.2s and fall into the hellbox with ticks. The colophon counts them ('Hellbox · 37 sorts'). Footnote §: 'The page is set in movable type. Try typing a word.'
moves.implementation:
- Keydown: skip e.isComposing, ctrl/meta/alt, editable targets and html.case-open. Accept letters and digits only, with a buffer of at most 12.
- A dictionary map dispatches to K2.setMode or to director cues.
- The stick is a fixed div of <b> sorts with scaleX(−1). On a match, flap() each sort with a 30ms stagger, then fire.
- KLEIN: 12–16 splats of radius 0.35·vmin on a jittered grid with ghost:true, with dye decay dropped to .35 for 2.5s and then restored to 1.15.
- GOLD: set uX to PIG.XB on paper areas (paper → Monogold, ink → navy) and add uLeaf. In the display shader, a hashed 18px Voronoi cell modulates the print threshold and per-cell brightness by ±6% to make leaf squares. Difference math is unchanged, and the IKB-band XB rects keep working.
- MAKE input: a command word both runs and becomes the LOUD word ('MAKE KLEIN LOUD').
- aria-live polite announces mode changes.
- The Ant plate stays IKB-only, which respects the gold-only-on-the-seal rule.
moves.phone: There is no hardware keyboard, so the MAKE ___ LOUD field is the stick. A quiet mono hint sits under the chips: 'Also try: KLEIN · GOLD · GRID · ELEVEN'. KLEIN uses the same splats; the 2D fallback uses big blots.
moves.perf_and_fallback:
- The stick is idle DOM.
- KLEIN costs the same as a busy brush for about 3s.
- No WebGL: 2D blots.
- Pigment off or reduced motion: KLEIN and GOLD only toast and change the mode label; nothing floods.
- Keys reach the page only after the iframe has focus, so every command also has a click route (console, MAKE input).

moves.name: DEMONSTRATION: the specimen performs itself when left alone (+ seeded sequencer)
moves.where: Global. Acts run in Hero, Strings, Work index, Board and Colophon. Never in Text, the case sheet, contact inputs or the plate.
moves.experience:
After 16s with no input on a showable section, the crop-mark rig detaches with the chip 'AUTO · move to take over' and performs the section like a foundry specimen film:
- Hero: sweeps the name (pluck), strikes R and then 4 (bursts), paints a ghost stroke in the margin.
- With sound on, the hero becomes a 7-step sequencer. The rig is the playhead; each step strikes a letter to 150/900 on a 16th-note grid at 92 BPM. The pattern is seeded from the plate number, so each visitor's page hums its own riff.
- Strings: two sweeps (a rising pentatonic run).
- Work: walks rows 01→05, showing every riso plate with slip.
- Board: idle tiles re-flap in place.
- Colophon: cycles MAKE NOISE / WAVES / HISTORY LOUD, knocks one letter loose and re-sets it.

Any input springs the rig back to the real pointer in 200ms, and every system settles on its own rest logic.
moves.phone:
- Same 16s idle rule.
- A 28px IKB hairline ring is the ghost finger (the rig is for fine pointers only).
- Acts use swipe-pluck, strike, the chips, and inline plate slip instead of the card walk.
- Never paints over copy.
moves.perf_and_fallback:
- Costs the same as manual interaction, only while idle, for at most 45s.
- Reduced motion: disabled.
- Sound off: visual only.
- Lenis absent: unaffected.
- Never runs in a hidden tab.

moves.name: VOLUME: the crescendo as a global axis (fader 0–10, 11 = LOUD MODE, console)
moves.where:
- Desktop: a 10-segment mono fader plus readout in the nav, between the folio and SOUND. Below 1100px it collapses to 'VOL 05', which opens the console.
- Phone: a bottom sheet in the menu.
- Keys 0–9, the composing stick, ELEVEN / Konami.
moves.experience:
The thesis becomes a control. VOL 05 is the specimen as designed.
- Drag down: every display line on the page (hero letters, tapes, work titles, threshold, board glyphs, LOUD lines, email, monogram) eases toward Thin Compressed 50/100 while staying fitted edge to edge.
- Drag up: toward Black Extended 150/900.
- Body copy and mono never move, so the page stays readable.
- Push past 10 and it clicks to 11, LOUD MODE: every display line goes to 150/900, the page shakes once (380ms), and a sub-bass hit plays if sound is on. An IKB burst fires from the fader, the folio reads 'p. 11/06 LOUD', and the toast says 'This one goes to eleven.' The physics letters get heavier and land harder.
- The console (click VOL) adds the Kinetik case's 2D axis pad (x = wdth target, y = wght target), a SLNT slider (synthetic skewX ±12, footnote *), presets WHISPER / SPEC / LOUD / CHAOS, and RESET. CHAOS gives every display line its own seeded random instance, still fitted: a ransom-note specimen.
- With sound on, master gain and the low-pass also follow VOL.
moves.implementation:
- K2.mode.vol is spring-animated to an amount a and a target instance T. One remap: K2.inst(w, g) → [w + (Tw − w)·a, g + (Tg − g)·a].
- CSS-driven display (tapes with --w/--g, row titles, thr words, email, monogram) moves to registered @property --vw, --vg, --va inside calc() in font-variation-settings.
- The ~18 JS fontVariationSettings writers route through K2.inst().
- Fit registry K2.fits = [{line, box}]. While vol animates, the read phase reads all widths once (one forced layout) and the write phase sets fs·cw/w. At rest there is no work.
- Hero: remap RAMP before the chain (the chain already conserves the measure).
- Stage C physics: wght-only remap while bodies are loose; full remap plus typeset() when they are home.
- Shake: translate on main.page only (the fixed layers are its siblings), with will-change only during the shake.
- CHAOS seed: mulberry32(plate number + index).
- Excluded: the manifesto (pre-broken lines), case copy, labels and inputs.
- After settling, call measurePins() once.
moves.phone:
- The sheet holds a full-width fader with 11 detents, with a haptic tick through the existing buzz policy when sound is on.
- Preset chips, and a 2D pad of about 200px.
- No rotary knobs.
moves.perf_and_fallback:
- Zero at rest.
- While dragging, one forced layout per frame for at most 12 fitted lines: about 1–2ms on desktop, about 3ms on a mid-range phone.
- No @property support: the CSS items step instead of tweening.
- Reduced motion: instant jumps, no shake.
- Highest-touch change in the plan: put it behind K2.mode, so it can be cut cleanly.

moves.name: STRING SNAP: the first-half peak you cause
moves.where: B2 Strings, on the crossing '+' node and on the tapes.
moves.implementation:
- Per tape, a snap state: two verlet chains of 16 nodes (half the tape's length each, gravity 2200px/s², 6 constraint iterations, damping .985), seeded from the current curve samples plus the flick velocity.
- Words sample position and angle from the chain polyline: the same per-word transform path with a different sampler.
- Re-string: blend from chain to rest curve over 2.4s with ease-out-back, Sound.tick ×6 rising, and a KS pluck at the end.
- Trigger: pointer drag velocity above 2800px/s on a tape, or a node click. 12s cooldown. Never from scroll alone.
- Goes through the director.
moves.phone: A thumb flick on a tape above the threshold snaps it; the horizontal pan is already captured with touch-action pan-y. The halves hang inside the field box.
moves.perf_and_fallback: 64 nodes for 2.4s costs about 0.05ms. Reduced motion: disabled, and the node click plucks instead.

moves.name: PULL-TO-REWIND lever: no dead end
moves.where: The foot REWIND bar, at maximum scroll.
moves.experience: At the very bottom, keep scrolling and the REWIND bar becomes a press lever. Its dot leaders fill left to right with ink and the label reads 'Keep pulling to rewind · 64%'. Let go and it springs back; reach 100% and the tape rewind fires. The page loops instead of ending.
moves.implementation:
- Arms only after the page has sat at max scroll for 800ms, and not while a colophon field has focus.
- Wheel deltaY, or touch overscroll distance at max, accumulates into pull, which decays at 900px/s.
- Thresholds: 1100px of wheel or 240px of touch, then Rewind.run().
- Progress goes to a CSS variable on the bar.
- The button stays the accessible control.
moves.phone: An overscroll drag at the bottom (touchmove while at max; iOS rubber-banding still reports it). Threshold 240px.
moves.perf_and_fallback: Trivial cost. Reduced motion: disabled, button only. The guards prevent accidental rewinds while reading the footnotes.

moves.name: NIGHT PRESS (opt-in, behind a flag)
moves.where: A console toggle, the composing-stick words NIGHT / DAY, and the phone menu.
moves.implementation:
- html[data-stock=night] swaps the values of --paper, --ink, --mute and --hair (the mute greys need night values that are contrast-checked).
- Canvases read colours from a K2.colors() getter and repaint on the mode event: the riso C object, board, flood and cursor chip. The plate stays paper, because it is a print.
- document.startViewTransition(() => set the attribute), with ::view-transition-new(root) animating clip-path inset(0 0 100% 0) → inset(0) over 900ms, plus a synced fixed .roller div.
- Fallback: swap at mid-roll under the roller.
- Pigment X and XB are unchanged.
moves.phone: Menu toggle, same roller.
moves.perf_and_fallback:
- A one-off snapshot, then static.
- Risk is in the many hard-coded canvas colours and selection styles, and in the arc inverting (paper → ink becomes ink → paper), which needs a design pass.
- Build last, or cut.

reject: Night Press following prefers-color-scheme dark by default: the first impression must be the designed paper → ink → IKB crescendo, and the spec asks for a single deliberate light look. Opt-in only.
Cursor glyph trail and type-brush variants: the pigment already is the trail. Two trails would fight, and the crop-mark rig is the cursor's identity.
Velocity-based global type stretch while scrolling: an Awwwards trope that breaks fitted measures and 'readable at rest' for little gain. The hero and strings already answer scroll velocity locally.

Letterpress platen as a section-to-section transition: a third full-screen blackout after the threshold zoom and the flood would flatten both, and it would delay the work index. The platen moves to the ending (Press Pull), where printing is the point.
Full-screen wipes between every section: same reason. Seams become lock-ups and downbeats; only the threshold and the flood stay full-screen events.
Rotary WDTH / WGHT / SLNT knobs: fiddly with a mouse and bad on touch. Use one VOL fader plus the existing Kinetik 2D pad and a slider.
Standalone always-on sequencer: sound is opt-in and rarely on. It is folded into the Demonstration (seeded riff) instead.
Konami code as the main route to LOUD: undiscoverable. VOL 11 is discoverable and funnier; Konami stays only as an alias.
Hellbox as a hidden page: it becomes the composing stick's discard animation plus a colophon counter, which is visible and costs nothing.

A second WebGL context, or new libraries (three.js, GSAP, Tone.js): nothing here needs them. The PROOF quiver and GOLD leaf are branches in the existing pigment display shader; everything else is 2D canvas, CSS or WebAudio.
'Save your plate' or any download or share-out: the artifact frame forbids downloads and window.open. The pressed and stamped plate is the souvenir on the page.
